payload.claim: `_review_change_lines` decides whether an ancestor changed REVIEW-shaping code by reading `spec.touches` straight from the spec file's frontmatter. For a bug-type spec, CONTEXT.md's own definition of `touches` says the declared set 'has none' at file level; DIAGNOSE proposes it per-run and `saffron/cell/session.py:2000-2006` says outright 'Latent: nothing writes it back yet' when that proposal is ratified. So a live bug-spec ancestor whose ratified touches actually included e.g. `saffron/phases/review.py` still shows `spec.touches == []` in its file, and this walk silently omits its `review:` line. Every fixture and test added by this diff uses `type: feature`, where touches are declared up front, so the gap never shows up under test but will under a real bug-spec ancestor, exactly the assumption-holds-in-fixtures-not-production case.
